blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Section 8(1) of the RTI Act, 2005 outlines specific categories of information exempted from public disclosure.
Cabinet papers, including records of deliberations of the Council of Ministers, are exempt until the decision is finalized and the matter is complete.
Section 9 empowers the Public Information Officer to reject a request if it involves copyright infringement of a non-State entity.
Section 24 exempts second-schedule intelligence and security agencies, except for matters pertaining to corruption and human rights violations.
A public authority may allow access to exempted information if the larger public interest in disclosure outweighs the harm to protected interests.

blocks.content: Notwithstanding anything in the Official Secrets Act, 1923, a public authority may allow access to information if public interest in disclosure outweighs the harm to the protected interests.

rows: Covers national security, fiduciary duty, trade secrets, and personal privacy.
Disclosable if public interest outweighs protected harm (Section 8(2)).
Records of deliberations of Council of Ministers and Secretaries.
Becomes public after the decision is taken and the matter is complete.
Intelligence and security bodies listed in the Second Schedule.
Non-exempt for allegations of corruption and human rights violations.

items: Allegations of corruption and human rights violations in exempted security agencies (Section 24) are NOT exempt from disclosure under RTI.
Information regarding human rights violations requires approval from the Information Commission and must be provided within 45 days.
Exemption under Section 8(1) generally ceases after 20 years, except for items affecting national security, parliamentary privilege, and Cabinet deliberations.
